title: Code Preview Build Plan

steps.name: The readability check
steps.summary: A new script, scripts/readability.py, checks every line a diff adds, in Python, JavaScript and C#. Names are whole words. Each line holds one statement, and a statement is never split across lines, even if that makes it long. Each part of a long condition gets a yes-or-no name. Each function opens with a plain sentence, and no logic is packed into a one-line lambda (a small unnamed function). Values sit inside f-strings or interpolated strings (strings with the value written in the text), and patterns are built from named pieces.
changes: Tests: each rule refuses a bad line and passes a good one, in Python, JavaScript and C#. More tests cover quoted text, comments, two quoted strings side by side on one line, older helpers and names that already existed.

The pattern builder: named pieces such as spaces, digits and capture(...). Patterns (regular expressions) are built from them, so each one reads as a sentence. It is the one file that holds raw pattern syntax.
The readability check reads a diff (a list of changed lines), finds which added lines are Python, JavaScript or C#, and checks each one against the rules.

What I have proven, and what I have not
Tested in scratch copies of the repo; nothing is in the plugin yet.

Proven: the full test suite passes 1,042 of 1,042 checks on the final copy, against 973 on the untouched copy. Every step's draft passes the readability check against the step before it. Plan mode checked all six drafts again while building this page. The coding standards text injected in a Unity and Node project measures 9,479 characters against its 9,500-character budget. Not yet run: the whole test suite for each of steps 2 to 5 on its own, although each step's own test files did pass. Also not proven: the real run in a scratch repo, which happens during the build. Issue #457 (Design loop fixes) is on another branch and also moves the version to 2.76.0, so whichever merges second takes the next version number.

Where the rules leave older code alone
New code follows every rule; older code it touches gets a readable name and is not rewritten.

Older helpers with short names, such as _mp and _loop_dir, get a readable name where new code calls them. A line like run_page_builder = _mp names each one once. Renaming them everywhere is issue #474 (A readable-code skill, and readable code across every repo the agent has touched). If the same diff block also removes a name, the name already existed, so the check leaves it alone. Only one line of existing code is shown on each side of a change, in grey. Git's diff markers, such as " b/" before a file's new path, are named constants with a comment. A list written with one whole item per line still counts as one statement per line. C# has no pattern builder yet, so a raw C# pattern is refused until the readable-code skill supplies one. Short connecting words such as "and" and "of" are fine inside a longer name. Comments are checked as ordinary sentences.
choices: How should #474 (A readable-code skill) and #475 (The design loop counts every issue opened during Plan as part of the current feature) stop blocking this approval?
Label them in progress until step 5 is built
I add `in progress` to #474 (A readable-code skill) and #475 with a comment on each saying why. Once step 5 is built, your Not part of line takes them out and I remove the label.
Close both as not planned, reopen after the merge
Closing each issue needs your own message, and both stop showing as open until they are reopened.
Your approval goes through the hooks installed now, which do not have step 5's fix yet. Option A keeps both issues open and explains the label in writing; option B hides two planned pieces of work.
